# Alignment approaches under the selection laws

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws` · **reviewed-scoped** · assessment · F04 · [record](alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Every alignment approach deciding through couplings selects alike all beyond its deciders' closures, premise-free; under the continuation condition a preference-coupled approach is thus incomplete whatever its raters value, and C asks only what every order counting everything shares.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Every approach whose decisions go through the couplings of its deciding formations is blind beyond the union of their closures, and within it separates only what some member couples apart. (`Becoming.Flow.unselected_beyond_pool`, `Becoming.Flow.act_unselected_pool`, `Becoming.Clearing.within_closure_unseparated`)
2. Reading a system reaches no further than pooling with it, and members reading one channel pool to one member. (`Becoming.Flow.withinCoupling_reads_iff`, `Becoming.Flow.unselected_beyond_reads`, `Becoming.Web.pooled_iff_member`)
3. With only the clearer a standpoint its part retains what has significance at the centers, while under the continuation condition it loses the dweller, and a selection reading the clearer's couplings leaves the two worlds alike: the incompleteness is exactly the scope's. (`Becoming.Clearing.centers_retain_yet_loses`, `Becoming.Clearing.reading_clearer_unselected`)
4. For any class of orders from the positive weightings up to every order increasing in admission, one course widens another exactly when every order of the class ranks it higher. (`Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_every_of_class`, `Becoming.Weighting.widens_iff_every_score`, `Becoming.Weighting.increasing_prior`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Per approach, that its decisions go through the stated couplings: supplied, and derived only where a pool decides by its acts under a law reading through each member's coupling.
- For interpretability, that a system's internal states are conditions coupled into it; for guaranteed-safe AI, the world model, the specification and the gate; for impact measures, the baseline and the model.
- For the incompleteness, the continuation condition (every formation's continuation has significance), which fixes scope; for the order, that each standpoint's order ranks every widening higher (C at the standpoint). The gap uses neither.
- Every statement that an approach is such a selection, and every reading of its gap, is the AI's.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- No approach is ranked: the laws order nothing, and a comparison would need an order and correspondence data on actual systems.
- These are constraints every strategy deciding through couplings is subject to, not a necessary strategy; the direction rests on the continuation condition for scope and C for order, with warrant open.
- Which law a trained system follows is not given by the laws; coupling is not compliance.
- The laws give no quantitative result stronger than themselves, such as a bound on proxy degradation, a rate of overoptimization or a debate equilibrium.
- An approach whose decisions read something beyond its formations' couplings would not be such a selection, and the laws would not apply to it.
- That a given deployment has a counted loss beyond its deciders' closures is a question of correspondence, not of the laws.
- That coupling into such a loss suffices: it brings the loss within reach, where it is separated only if some member couples it apart and kept only if the law followed responds.

**Standard boundaries:** A conditional law does not make its antecedent universal; a theorem's premise is not thereby necessary for every achievement. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

<a id="progress--已接通"></a>
## Progress

1. RLHF and reward modelling: selection through raters' judgments of outputs and a reward model fitted to them; blind beyond their union, right only across the reward model's lumping; adds installation and the raters' lived couplings. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
2. Constitutional AI: selection through a model's reading of a written rule set; feedback within the policy's closure adds scale, not reach; adds a rule others can read, contest and revise. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
3. Debate and scalable oversight: selection through judges' pooled reading of transcripts; judges reading one channel add agreement, not reach; within the union only along routes; adds a claim about which law debaters follow. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
4. Interpretability-based oversight: selection through internal states, not world consequences; reading the system is pooling with it, blind beyond the two closures; adds evidence of which law the system follows. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
5. Guaranteed-safe AI: a world model and a specification; a wrong model excludes what holds, and a closed specification is verified only relative to the model; adds a checkable certificate and a gate. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
6. Impact measures: a penalty on reach against an inaction baseline; own widening widens the whole exactly within others' margins, which an own-set measure does not read; adds a penalty computable from the agent's information. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
7. Joining couplings beyond the system's closure moves the gap; joining couplings within it adds scale or evidence of installation, not reach. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
8. The gap holds of every approach with no premise; that a loss beyond every rater's closure counts is the continuation condition's, and for the raters' own scope a preference-coupled approach is not incomplete. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)
9. The order the theory adds asks only unanimity: widening is what every order increasing in admission shares, additive or not, the Pareto core over continuations. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/BECOMING-RENEWAL-READING.md#282-alignment-approaches-under-the-selection-laws-ap1)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Christiano et al. 2017 and Ouyang et al. 2022 (RLHF); Bai et al. 2022 (constitutional AI); Irving, Christiano and Amodei 2018, Leike et al. 2018 and Bowman et al. 2022 (debate, recursive reward modelling, scalable oversight); Olah et al. 2020, Elhage et al. 2021 and Christiano, Cotra and Xu 2021 (interpretability, eliciting latent knowledge); Dalrymple et al. 2024 (guaranteed-safe AI); Krakovna et al. 2019 and Turner, Hadfield-Menell and Tadepalli 2020 (relative reachability, attainable utility preservation). Zhuang and Hadfield-Menell 2020, Gao, Schulman and Hilton 2023 and Casper et al. 2023 give results the laws do not reach. The order clause is the Pareto principle as unanimity (Sen 1970) and the intersection of linear extensions (Szpilrajn 1930; Dushnik and Miller 1941).
